current.text: He is a projected starter in a frontcourt with Jarrett Allen, next to James Harden, Donovan Mitchell and Peyton Watson.

It is not clear whether Kenny Atkinson will use him more at center in smaller lineups or lean on Allen and Harden pick-and-rolls. After the Peyton Watson trade, Cleveland may close games with Mobley at center.
Cleveland's big-man depth is very thin. Behind Mobley and Allen there is only Thomas Bryant, then Ernest Udeh Jr. and Khalifa Diop. Dean Wade is gone.
With Harden there for a full season, more Cavs players need the ball.
The experts disagree on a usage jump. One expert sees this as a big year for him on offense. Another is not sold on a big usage bump.

Last season was a down year. He had two calf strains, came back early and played on a minutes restriction. His free throw collapse was the main reason his fantasy value fell. He looked better in the playoffs.
Last season he finished 41st in category leagues and 29th in points leagues. His usage was 22.
After two straight seasons at 37% from three, he shot under 30% last season.
One expert expects his three-point percentage to bounce back toward 33 to 34%.

The experts disagree on his free throws this season. Some expect them to stay bad and would treat any improvement as a bonus. Others say the drop had no clear cause, could go either way, and they are not ready to call him a bad free throw shooter.
In recent mocks he went at pick 25, the earliest one expert has seen, and at pick 34 in a points mock. In an auction mock he went for 27 USD, a bit above the expected mid 20s USD.

Most experts are fine with his price around pick 30 and in the mid 20s USD. One sees him as a mid third to early fourth round pick in categories. Another is below consensus and calls him slightly overvalued.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With a March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and then 2 games in our playoff weeks. The two-game week is the final, in the week starting March 22.
The Cavs' playoff schedule is a minor concern for him. The two-game final week is a borderline factor.
He has no current injury concerns.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games. Coach Kenny Atkinson is under pressure.

durable.text: Blocks are his standout category, far above the top 250 pool. He also gives strong FG% on good volume and strong rebounds.
His FT% is a clear weakness on real volume and hurts a team's FT%.
His free throw shooting will never be excellent, though it could improve.
He is an elite defender with a high floor and is a good passer out of the pocket. The open question is whether his offense takes the next step.
He is 25 and not yet at his peak. He could become a 20-point scorer with two blocks per game.
He has a history of lower body injuries, including two calf strains last season.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both rank him 27th, with values of 30 and 27 USD and average costs of 26.7 and 21.9 USD. Experts see him as fair around pick 30, so 25 to 30 USD is a sensible range. That is well below the 36 USD our league paid last season. He fits punt FT% builds best, since his blocks, rebounds and FG% carry value without his free throws. Early in the season, watch whether his FT% gets back toward 70% and his three-point shooting toward 33%. Also check whether he plays more center minutes and whether he sits back-to-backs on a team with the most in the league.
